About Climate City

A new way to live. A shared future to build.

Explore our sectors

An African vision
for a city that works better.

Rooted in Nigeria. Designed around the lives and landscapes that sustain us.

Climate City is a proposed sustainable community in Nasarawa State, Nigeria, powered by Mikoshel. It brings housing, essential services, enterprise and culture into one connected plan, with the ambition to make resource-conscious living practical, comfortable and economically productive.

Our philosophy begins with a simple responsibility: the places we build should improve people’s lives while respecting the land and resources they depend on. That means considering the home, the street, the workplace and the wider landscape together—from shade and natural ventilation to reliable services, responsible water use and access to everyday needs.

Environmental care and economic opportunity belong in the same conversation. We aim to create space for local businesses, skilled work, education and responsible investment, alongside mixed-income homes and shared public places. Host communities, African enterprise and cultural identity are central to that ambition.

The landscape is part of the city’s infrastructure. Native and climate-adapted planting, connected habitats and site-appropriate water systems will guide a plan that responds to local ecology. Schools, healthcare, markets and cultural destinations will give residents and visitors reasons to learn, work and spend time here.

Starting in Nigeria, we want to develop a model of urban living that other African communities can learn from and adapt. Delivery will be phased, with site studies, specialist partnerships and measurable performance shaping how the vision becomes reality.

How each sector contributes

Each part of Climate City has a role in reducing resource use, strengthening climate resilience or improving community wellbeing. These proposed approaches will guide phased development.

01Homes and neighbourhoods

Mixed-income apartments and courtyard homes will provide shelter close to everyday services. Shade, natural ventilation, efficient cooling and materials selected for durability and lower embodied carbon can reduce energy demand and construction impacts while supporting comfortable living.

02Nature and wildlife conservation

Dense, site-appropriate planting and connected habitats will support wildlife, provide shade and help store carbon as vegetation matures. Native and non-invasive, climate-adapted species will guide a landscape designed around existing ecology, with conservation trails and opportunities to learn about nature.

03Clean energy

Solar power, battery storage and managed distribution, supported by the grid, will help reduce dependence on fossil-fuel electricity. Efficient appliances, passive design and smart meters will help residents and businesses reduce demand and manage energy costs.

04Water and circular systems

Rainwater capture, efficient fixtures, wastewater treatment and safe reuse will help conserve freshwater. Site-suitable lakes, wetlands and drainage will support stormwater management and habitats. Waste sorting, reuse, recycling and organics recovery will reduce disposal, with separate specialist handling for clinical and hazardous waste.

05Mobility and digital services

Shaded walking routes, cycle paths and electric shuttles will connect homes with work, learning and leisure, helping reduce car dependence. Smart metering and maintenance systems will help identify leaks, energy waste and service faults, making the city easier to manage and live in.

06Food systems and livelihoods

Gardens, greenhouses, orchards and farmer partnerships will connect the city to fresh food and local livelihoods. Efficient irrigation, compost use and well-managed cold storage can conserve resources and reduce food loss. Any ranch activities will need their own methane, manure and land-management measures.

07Education and research

Schools, technical training, public libraries and outdoor reading gardens will build skills for a greener economy. Research partnerships will test practical approaches to clean energy, water efficiency and climate adaptation, helping share lessons with communities across Africa.

08Healthcare and wellbeing

Planned clinics and a phased hospital opportunity will bring diagnostics, primary and specialist care closer to residents and visitors. Qualified clinical partners will guide services, including evidence-based natural and complementary care where appropriate. Efficient facilities, reliable clean power and safe clinical-waste management will support responsible operations.

09Enterprise and civic life

Markets, shops, offices and civic spaces will create local jobs and put services within easier reach. Shared infrastructure, efficient cold storage, reusable packaging and coordinated deliveries can reduce waste and avoid unnecessary journeys while strengthening local businesses.

10African heritage and culture

A proposed museum and heritage galleries will preserve and share African stories, with authentic artefacts sourced through documented acquisitions, loans and cultural partnerships. Resource-efficient exhibition spaces and local creative enterprise will connect heritage preservation with education, livelihoods and responsible tourism.

11Hospitality and international exchange

Hotels, proposed diplomatic apartments and shared meeting spaces will offer a home away from home for tourists, visiting professionals and international guests. Efficient cooling, water-saving systems, local sourcing and shared transport will help manage the environmental footprint of hospitality while supporting cultural exchange and trade.

12Sport and active living

Walking trails, sports grounds, swimming and shared recreation facilities will support healthier lives close to home. Efficient lighting, responsible water use and habitat-sensitive siting will guide delivery; wider golf and equestrian ambitions will depend on suitable sites and resource capacity.

Making the ambition measurable

Our aim is to track whole-life carbon alongside energy, water, waste, canopy cover, mobility and housing affordability. Our goal includes pursuing high LEED ratings, with a Platinum ambition for suitable projects, subject to independent assessment and certification.

Climate City is in pre-development. Final facilities, capacities and timelines will be shaped by site studies, approvals, funding and specialist partnerships.

A place to call home. A future to build together.

About Mikoshel

Mikoshel is a Nigerian diversified business company with its roots in real estate and property investment. The business began in 2020 and has expanded into China importation, international sourcing and automotive services.

Real estate remains the foundation of the business. Our international trade and automotive activities extend this foundation, connecting customers with property opportunities, products and vehicles from international markets.

We bring these activities together through shared business relationships, sourcing experience and a commitment to long-term value for customers, investors and partners.

Investor Relations
